full_judgment:
MM Huq, J. : This is an application for review of our Judgment dated 4.11.93 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 444 of 1992 under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure." 

 2. In the instant case the girl was kept in judicial custody under order of the learned Sessions Judge. One Samad Ahmed claiming himself as the husband of the girl moved that application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. The present petitioner Md. Momtazullah, the father of the girl, was the opposite-party No. 2 in that application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Under order of this court notice was served upon this Md. Momtazullah by special messenger. At the time of hearing of the Rule, this father Md. Momtazullah did not appear. Under order of this court the girl was produced before us. On considering the materials on record and after seeing the appearance of the girl this court by the judgment dated 4.11.92 made the Rule absolute finding the girl major and allowed her to go anywhere she liked. 

 3. The present petitioner Md. Momtazullah was the opposite-party No. 2 and is also the father of the girl. This petitioner filed an application for review of our judgment dated 4.11.92. Mr. Moazzam Hossain the learned Deputy Attorney-General representing the State, submits that such a review application is a clear bar under section 369 of the Code of Criminal Procedure inasmuch as the judgment has been passed on merit of the case and it has already been signed by both the judges of the Division Bench. The learned Advocate Mr. Md. Shahajahen, appearing for the present petitioner, submits that the criminal case started against the accused in connection with taking away of the girl is still pending in the trial Court and that has not yet been disposed of and for this reason this application for review is maintainable before this court. We are unable to accept the above contention of the learned Advocate in view of the fact that the husband of the girl moved this court under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule and in that Rule we only considered the question of majority and minority of the girl. On the basis of the materials on record and considering the orders passed by the two courts below this court expressed its view that the girl is major Pendency of the criminal case before the learned Magistrate will not in any way give the present petitioner locus standi to file the present application for review in view of the fact that this is totally contrary to the provisions of section 369 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We are of the view that the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 444 of 1992 was decided on its own merit and there is nothing to review in this matter. In the judgment this court had not made any observation regarding the merit of the Pending criminal case.
